answer: Each Ember Cartographer node earns a reputation token stamped with a unique saffron‑colored hash that ages like copper in a tide of transactions; the token’s weight grows each block of verified work and halves after thirty days of inactivity. When a new identity appears it must purchase an initial token bundle, but to match the influence of an older node it must repeatedly fund the aging process, a cost that scales exponentially with the desired reputation level.
